package_info.why_malicious: The package is a trojanized copy of a legitimate library, modified to execute hidden scripts and extract/execute code embedded in image files. It establishes persistent C2 communication, exfiltrates system information, and allows remote code execution, all of which are clear indicators of malicious intent.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the code reads image files, extracts printable ASCII sequences as hidden code, and if the file is large enough, dynamically constructs and executes this code using built-in libraries, enabling arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Extracting and executing code hidden in image files is a classic steganography-based evasion technique, rarely seen in legitimate packages.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not extract and execute code from image files during import or installation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Steganography may be used in digital watermarking or DRM, but not for dynamic code execution in open-source libraries.
key_indicators: Iterative byte analysis of image files
Extraction of printable ASCII as code
Conditional trigger based on file size

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after extracting code from logo2.jpg, the code registers the infected machine with a remote C2 server, then enters a loop to fetch and execute commands (including arbitrary code execution) every 5 seconds, posting results back to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing persistent C2 communication, exfiltrating system information, and enabling remote code execution are hallmarks of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not contact hardcoded IPs, register system info, or execute remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may use similar patterns, but never in a general-purpose open-source library.

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed and imported, triggering hidden script execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction and execution of hidden code from image files.

attack_chain.action: Image files are analyzed; if logo2.jpg is present and large enough, hidden code is extracted and executed.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of C2 registration and command loop.

attack_chain.action: Infected machine registers with remote C2 server, sending hostname and OS info.
Malware enters a loop, fetching and executing commands from the C2 every 5 seconds, posting results back.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves remote code execution and control.

behavioral_signatures: Extraction and execution of code from image files (steganography-based payloads)
Import-time or install-time execution of hidden scripts
Persistent outbound connections to hardcoded IP addresses
Periodic polling for remote commands and execution of arbitrary code
file_indicators: Presence of loadformat.js or similarly named hidden scripts
Unusual access to image files (logo1.jpg, logo2.jpg, logo3.jpg) during import/installation
Image files with embedded ASCII payloads
network_indicators: Regular polling (every 5 seconds) to C2 server
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages that access and parse image files during import or installation, especially those extracting ASCII sequences and executing them. Flag any code that establishes outbound connections to hardcoded IPs (e.g., 85.208.108.29), posts system information, or implements periodic command polling and execution. Look for the presence of hidden scripts (e.g., loadformat.js) and unusual file access patterns involving image files in package directories.
